answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a island as the anchor of the cost.
